sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Arctostaphylos uva-ursi, bearberry, is a creeping evergreen subshrub, usually under about 15 cm high, with leathery leaves and small urn-shaped pinkish flowers. It occurs across cool temperate and subarctic regions of the Northern Hemisphere. Red fruits are usually about 6–10 mm across.

sections.title: Fruit and uses
sections.text: The ripe berries are edible but mealy and are often cooked or dried; local traditions vary. Leaves have medicinal uses, but this is not a safety endorsement for home treatment. The plate's low mat, small leaves and red berries fit the species.
